Pair baseline and candidate trajectories on an explicit key

Source: R/pair-trajectories.R
pair_trajectories.Rd

pair_trajectories() matches the trajectories of two saved investigations case by case. It reads recorded identities only: it never runs a solver, a scorer, or a model, and it never matches by position. Every trajectory of both investigations appears in exactly one of the returned tables.

Usage

pair_trajectories(
  baseline,
  candidate,
  by,
  dataset_version = NULL,
  scorers = NULL
)

Arguments

baseline, candidate

Saved investigations from investigation_snapshot() or read_investigation(). A saved investigation carries the snapshot identity and the frozen analysis that a comparison cites.

by

Key columns: "sample_id", optionally with "task_id" and "epoch". There is no default.

dataset_version

The dataset version of both sides as one string, or a character vector named baseline and candidate. NULL leaves it undeclared.

scorers

Scorer declarations from comparison_scorer(): a list applied to both sides, or a list with baseline and candidate lists when the sides differ.

Value

A scans_pairing value: a list of ordinary tibbles and the two investigations.

  • key: by and the declared dataset versions.

  • snapshots: one row per side with snapshot and revision identifiers.

  • pairs: one row per matched case with both trajectory identities.

  • only_baseline, only_candidate: cases present on one side.

  • duplicates: every trajectory whose key occurs more than once on either side, with the count on each side.

  • missing_key: trajectories lacking a key value, and which one.

  • scorers: recorded and declared scorer attributes per side.

  • outcome_pairs: one row per pair and scorer with compatibility ("compatible", "incompatible", "unknown", or "missing") and the reason.

Cases and keys

A case is one sample of one dataset version. by names the recorded identity columns of trajectory_info() that identify it and must include "sample_id". Add "task_id" when an investigation holds several tasks. Add "epoch" when a sample was run more than once: epoch k of the baseline then pairs with epoch k of the candidate. Without "epoch" in the key, repeated epochs of a sample are duplicates and are reported, not reduced to one.

vitals does not record a dataset version, so the caller declares it. Cases pair only when both sides declare the same version. A side without a declared version has every trajectory reported as missing a key value.

Scorers

Outcomes pair only when scorer identity, version, scale, and direction agree on both sides. vitals records a scorer label (the expression passed as scorer) and, for an ordered factor score, its levels in order. It records no scorer version and no direction for numeric or logical scores. Declare what the record lacks with comparison_scorer(). An undeclared attribute stays unknown, and an unknown or disagreeing scorer pair is reported in outcome_pairs with its reason. It is never coerced.

See also

compare_trajectories() for per-case changes.

Examples

bundle <- TrajectoryBundle(
  data.frame(
    trajectory_id = c("a", "b"),
    sample_id = c("case-1", "case-2"),
    source_type = "manual",
    status = "completed"
  ),
  data.frame(),
  data.frame()
)
if (rlang::is_installed(c("digest", "jsonlite"))) {
  baseline <- investigation_snapshot(bundle, application = "Baseline")
  candidate <- investigation_snapshot(
    bundle,
    trajectory_ids = "a",
    application = "Candidate"
  )
  pairing <- pair_trajectories(
    baseline,
    candidate,
    by = "sample_id",
    dataset_version = "2026-11"
  )
  pairing$pairs
  pairing$only_baseline
}
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   dataset_version task_id sample_id epoch trajectory_id
#>   <chr>           <chr>   <chr>     <int> <chr>        
#> 1 2026-11         NA      case-2       NA b
